chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Umarah, from a man, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

When it was the night in which 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام had been promised, he said to Muhammad عليه السلام: “O my son, get me water for wudu (ablution).” He said: “So I arose and brought him water for wudu (ablution).” He said: “I do not want this, for there is something dead in it.”

He said: “So I went out and brought the lamp, and there was a dead mouse in it. So I brought him other water for wudu (ablution). Then he said: ‘O my son, this is the night that I was promised.’ He then gave instructions concerning his she-camel: that an enclosure be made for her and that fodder be set out for her. So she was placed in it.”

He said: “It was not long before she came out until she reached the grave. She struck with her chest, moaned, and her eyes overflowed. Then Muhammad ibn 'Ali was informed, and it was said to him: ‘The she-camel has gone out.’ So he went to her and said: ‘Hush, now rise; may Allah bless you.’ But she did not do so. Then he said: ‘He used to go out upon her to Makkah, hanging the whip on the saddle, yet he would not strike her until he entered al-Madinah.’”

He said: “And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام would go out in the dark night carrying a sack containing purses of dinars and dirhams, going from door to door, knocking, then giving to whoever came out to him. So when 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام passed away, they missed that, and they came to know that it had been 'Ali عليه السلام who used to do it.”

key_terms.الصُّرَرُ: small purses or packets of money
key_terms.اللَّيْلَةِ الظَّلْمَاءِ: the dark night in which he went out secretly
key_terms.النَّاقَةَ: the she-camel of Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave to which the she-camel came
key_terms.فَأْرَةٌ مَيِّتَةٌ: a dead mouse found in the water

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the final night and hidden charity of Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the final night of Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام, his awareness of his appointed death, and details from his conduct and character. It also preserves reports of his gentleness toward animals and his hidden charity to the people at night, which became known only after his passing.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Bin Aamir, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq Bin Sa’ad, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abu Umara, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

When it was the night in which Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws was to pass away, heasws said to Muhammadasws: ‘O myasws sonasws! Prepare the Wudou (ablution water) for me’. So heasws said: ‘So Iasws arose but (someone) brought to himasws with the (water for) Wudou’. But heasws said: ‘This is not proper for there is something dead in it’.

Heasws said: ‘So Iasws went out and came with the lantern, and there was a dead rat in it. So Iasws brought to himasws with Wudou (water) other than it. So heasws said: ‘O myasws sonasws”. This is the night which Iasws have been Promised it’. So heasws bequeathed with hisasws she-camel, and a stable be made for her and that feed should be established for her’. So Iasws made her to be in it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So it was not long before she exited until she came to the grave, and she struck herself by its side and rolled over it, and her eyes were flooded. So they came to Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and said to him<sup>asws</sup> that the she-camel had gone out. So he<sup>asws</sup> went over to her and said: ‘Calm down now, arise, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you!’ But she did not do so. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And even when he (Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>) went out to Makkah upon her, so he<sup>asws</sup> would hang the whip upon the carriage, and he<sup>asws</sup> would not whip her until he<sup>asws</sup> entered Al-Medina’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it was so that Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> would go out during the dark night, so he<sup>asws</sup> would carry the sack in which would be the packets of Dinars and Dirhams, until he<sup>asws</sup> would come upon door after door, so he<sup>asws</sup> would know upon it, then he<sup>asws</sup> would give it to the one who came out to him<sup>asws</sup>. So when Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> passed away, that was missed, and they came to know that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was the one doing it’.
en.sarwar: 4. al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amir has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa‘d from Su‘dan ibn Muslim from abu ‘Imara from a man from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“When it was the night wherein Ali ibnhy (a.s.) would pass away he asked his Muhammad (a.s.), his son, “Son bring me water for Wudu (cleaning for prayer). Muhammad has said, “I then brought water for him.” He said, “I do not like this water. There is something dead in it.”

I then brought the water in the light and found a dead mouse in it. I then brought him other water. He said, “Son this is the night in which I am promise to be taken out of this world. He explained his recommendations about his she camel and that a stable be prepared for her and that she is fed properly and I personally did so.

Very shortly there after she came out of the stable and reached the grave, placed her neck on it, rolled her bodyon the ground and her eyes had become full of tears. Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.) was informed that the she camel had gone. He came to her and said, “Control your emotion and get up, may Allah grant you good fortune. She would not do so. The Imam (a.s.) has said, “When he would take the camel to Makka, he would hang the whip from the luggage and would not use it until he would return to Madina.”

The Imam (a.s.) has said, “Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) would come out in the dark night with a sack containing Darahim and Dananir ( units of money) and would go door to door, knock them and gave a certain amount to the person that would come. When Ali ibn al-Husayn died these people would see the person with money and then they realized that Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) must have been the distributor of money among them.”
